reason: I downloaded Project Gutenberg etext 8120 myself. Its title page reads Third Edition Enlarged, ed. Rev. Fr. Benedict Zimmerman, London: Thomas Baker, with the Zimmerman introduction dated 16 July 1904 and the imprimatur 27 Sept. 1904, and the translator is David Lewis (the first edition was 1870, the second 1888). Under the heading Chapter XI (Why Men Do Not Attain Quickly to the Perfect Love of God. Of Four Degrees of Prayer. Of the First Degree), paragraph 10 opens: A beginner must look upon himself as making a garden, wherein our Lord may take His delight, but in a soil unfruitful, and abounding in weeds. His Majesty roots up the weeds, and has to plant good herbs. That matches the card to the letter, commas and capitals included, so ch. XI, section 10 is right and the wording is Lewis's own, not drift from another translator such as Peers or Cohen. The attribution is right: Teresa speaks in her own voice, so no speaker is owed, and nothing on the misattribution list touches it. shipped.js: not shipped, no near opening, Teresa at 0 of 3, not banned. In scope: a spiritual autobiography, not scripture or liturgy, like Julian of Norwich and Augustine already in the year. Publishable, ends in a full stop, prose kept as prose. The source line is 103 characters, leads with the name, has no dash, and names the translator and the 1904 edition whose wording it uses. Fame holds: the garden watered four ways is the image the Life is known by, and this sentence opens it. Two soft points, neither a refutation: the lines are religious (our Lord, His Majesty), which the Classics already allows; and the house has tagged the Confessions, the nearest analogue, as Philosophy, so the editor may prefer Philosophy over Essay for consistency.
